AMPIN Energy Green Private Limited, 2. AMPIN Energy Green Three Private Limited

Shri Suhael Bhuttan, Advocate, AMPIN
Ms. Pallavi Saigal, Advocate, CTUIL
ORDER
The AMPIN Energy Green Private Limited (formerly known as AMP Energy Green
private Limited) (“AMPIN Green”) and AMPIN Energy Green Three Private Limited
(“AMPIN Three”) (hereinafter referred to as the “Petitioners”) had filed the present Petition
seeking extension of Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCOD) for 50 MW Wind-
Solar Hybrid Project having connectivity at Fatehgarh-lV ISTS Pooling Station until
28.02.2026 and consequent waiver from payment of ISTS Charges under Regulation
13(2)(h)(ii) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State
Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the “2020
Sharing regulations”). The Petitioners have made the following prayers:
(a) Allow the present Petition.
(b) Approve the Recommendation Report of the CERC Committee dated 26.03.2026 in
respect of the Petitioner's 50 MW Wind-Solar Hybrid Project;
(c) Grant extension of the Project’s Scheduled Commercial Operation Date until the actual
Commercial Operation Date being 28.02.2026;
(d) Hold and declare that the Petitioner is entitled to a 100% waiver of Inter-State
Transmission System charges as if the project had achieved COD on or before
30.06.2025 in terms of Office Order dated 30.07.2025 (and addendum thereto);
AND/OR
(e) Pass any such further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in
the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Submission by the Petitioner:
2. The Petitioners have mainly submitted as under:
(a) The present Petition has been filed seeking extension of SCOD until 28.02.2026, for
the purpose of waiver of Inter-State Transmission System (“ISTS”) charges for 50 MW
Project under Regulation 13(2)(h)(ii) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations read with Office
Order dated 30.07.2025 and Addendum dated 14.01.2026 issued by this Commission.
(b) This Commission has constituted a “Committee for recommending Extension of Time
in SCOD for the specific projects” (“Committee”) to conduct a prudence check of the
applications submitted by Renewable Energy Generating Station ("REGS") and to
recommend whether a project is entitled to the extension of SCOD as sought, in cases
Order in Petition No. 228/MP/2026 Page 2

(q) In light of the above, AMPIN Green is fully entitled to the benefit of extension of SCOD
and the consequential waiver of ISTS charges, as if the Project had achieved COD
within the originally stipulated timelines.
Hearing dated 25.05.2026
3. The extracts of the RoP for the hearing dated 25.05.2026 are as under:
“The learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the present Petition has been filed
seeking extension of the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date for the Petitioners’ 50 MW
Wind-Solar Hybrid Project having connectivity at Fatehgarh lV ISTS Pooling Station until
28.02.2026 and consequent waiver from payment of the ISTS Charges under Regulation
13(2)(h)(ii) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State
Transmission Charges and Losses) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2025 read with this
Commission’s Office Order dated 30.07.2025 and its addendum dated 14.01.2026 and
Committee Recommendation Report dated 26.03.2026.
2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under:
(a) Admit and issue notice to the Respondent.
(b) The Respondent to file its reply, if any, within two weeks with a copy to the Petitioners,
who may file their rejoinder, if any, within a week thereafter.”
Hearing dated 29.06.2026
4. The extracts of the RoP for the hearing dated 29.06.2026 are as under:
“The learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the present Petition has been filed
seeking extension of the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date for the Petitioners’ 50 MW
Wind-Solar Hybrid Project having connectivity at Fatehgarh lV ISTS Pooling Station until
28.02.2026 and consequent waiver from the payment of the ISTS Charges under Regulation
13(2)(h)(ii) of the Sharing Regulations read with this Commission’s Office Order dated
30.07.2025 and its addendum dated 14.01.2026 and Committee’s Recommendation Report
dated 26.03.2026. The learned counsel submitted that the Respondent/CTUIL has not filed any
reply, and the matter may accordingly be reserved for order.
2. The learned counsel for the Respondent/CTUIL submitted that CTUIL does not wish to file
any reply in the matter.
3. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission
directed the Respondent/CTUIL to file an affidavit within a week clarifying whether the GNA has
been made effective for the Petitioner. If yes, the date from which the GNA has been made
effective and if not, the status of the transmission system which is required for making the GNA
effective for the Petitioner’s Project.
4. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matter for order.”
Submissions of CTUIL in compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 29.06.2026:
5. CTUIL vide affidavit dated 07.08.2026 submitted as under:
(a) The Petitioner’s Connectivity has not been made effective, and the anticipated date of
effectiveness of the subject Connectivity is 28.02.2027, as per the minutes of the 38th
Order in Petition No. 228/MP/2026 Page 5

14. In view of the above discussions, we are of the considered view that the Petitioner
AMPIN Green’s project shall be eligible for waiver of inter-state transmission charges,
as if the project had achieved COD on or before 30.06.2025 in terms of Regulation
13(2)(h) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations.
15. The Petition No. 228/MP/2026 stands disposed of in terms of the above.
Sd/ Sd/ Sd/ Sd/
(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V) (Jishnu Barua)
Member Member Member Chairperson

ORDER
This petition has been filed by the P etitioner, NTPC Limited (in short, ‘NTPC’),
for approval of the tariff of Singrauli Super Thermal Power Station (2000 MW) (in short,
‘the generating station’) for the period 2024-29, in accordance with the provisions of
the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2024 (in short ‘, the 2024 Tariff Regulations’).
2. The generating station has a total capacity of 2000 MW, comprising five units
of 200 MW each and two units of 500 MW each. The dates of commissioning of the
various units and that of the generating station are as under:
Unit CoD
Unit – I 1.6.1982
Unit – II 1.2.1983
Unit – III 1.7.1983
Unit – IV 1.1.1984
Unit – V 1.6.1984
Unit – VI 1.7.1987
Unit – VII/ Generating Station 1.5.1988
3. The Commission, vide its order dated 16.8.2026 in Petition No. 648/GT/2025,
had revised the tariff of the generating station for the period 2019-24 after a truing-up
Order in Petition No. 647/GT/2025 Page 2 of 57

since ash transportation charges are recurring in nature and the Petitioner has been
incurring the same at the generating station in the current tariff period also, grave
prejudice would be caused to the beneficiaries in case the Commission does not
permit/allow the Petitioner to recover fly ash transportation charges on the issuance
of this tariff order, because in that case the beneficiaries would be foisted with
additional liability of interest payment. The Petitioner has thus prayed to allow the
recovery of ash transportation charges on a monthly basis, subject to truing up at the
end of the 2024-29 period.
88. The Petitioner has also submitted that it has filed Petition No. 227/MP/2024
seeking recovery of fly ash transportation charges, which, as on date, is pending
disposal before the Commission. Reliance has also been placed by the Petitioner on
the order of the Commission dated 28.10.2022 in Petition No. 205/MP/2021 wherein
the Commission has considered the difficulties being faced by the Petitioner and
allowed the billing and recovery of the said expenses on a monthly basis for the period
2019-24.
89. The Respondents, TPDPL, BRPL, and BYPL, vide their respective replies,
have submitted that the Petitioner’s claim for recovery of ash transportation charges
through monthly billing is premature and contrary to the framework under the 2024
Tariff Regulations, which specifically requires that such claims be examined under
Regulation 36(1)(6) on the basis of a detailed prudence check. The earlier Order dated
28.10.2022 in Petition No. 205/MP/2021, relied upon by the Petitioner, is
distinguishable, and the issue is already sub judice in Petition No. 227/MP/2024.
Further, the Petitioner failed to disclose essential plant-wise data and revenue earned
from sale of fly ash; any recovery of gross transportation costs without adjusting
corresponding revenue would result in unjust enrichment.
Order in Petition No. 647/GT/2025 Page 43 of 57

reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the
present Petition, directly from the beneficiaries on a pro-rata basis in accordance with
Regulation 94(2) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations.
125. Similarly, RLDC Fees & Charges paid by the Petitioner under the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Fees and Charges of Regional Load Dispatch
Centre and other related matters) Regulations, 2009, shall be recovered from the
